alternatives.reason: project.yaml is a declared source of the demo Context Pack, which records a per-file content_hash. No generator exists to re-hash the pack, so any edit turns the pack STALE and breaks tests/http and tests/registry, as the PR #22 README edit did. The topology API exists to change environments at runtime, so this record uses it and leaves the governed Project untouched.

It would give a real OCI digest, but it ties the gate to a container runtime, needs socket access from the ContextRail process and still has no registry to compare against. DR-015 already accepts the go-run path as a first-class local run; a binary digest is the matching identity for it.

DR-015 rejected declared-only local records because they cannot exercise the parts of the gate that read a live service: healthz, revision identity and digest match. G4 asks for drift checks that actually fire.

architecture_impact: Each local environment is a separate process of the same built binary on its own loopback port, labelled by ORDER_PORTAL_ENV, so staging and prod-demo are told apart by what each instance reports about itself, not only by the port it was started on (roadmap §8 open question, DR-015 unknown).

A local instance carries two identities on /healthz: revision (<environment>-<start time>-<pid>, new on every start) and build_digest (sha256 of the running executable). The build digest is a local binary digest, not an OCI image digest; it is compared with the image_digest field of the build evidence only because both name the bytes that run.

release.Observer is a new interface; release.LocalReadBack is its only implementation. It accepts only loopback hosts (127.0.0.0/8, ::1, localhost), http or https, a bare origin without user info, query or fragment, never follows a redirect, uses a 5 second timeout and reads at most 64 KiB of /healthz.

A DeploymentRequest with source "local" must leave revision, deployed_digest, deployed_target_ref, deployed_config_hash and smoke empty and give service_url; ContextRail fills them from the read-back. The observed target_ref is derived as local/<service>-<environment> from the instance's own answer. An unreachable or unhealthy instance yields a smoke FAIL with the reason in smoke.detail, so the attempt is PROMOTION_FAILED with a receipt, never a silent pass.
The idempotency replay check runs before the read-back, so a retry with the same key returns the recorded attempt and receipt without reading the instance again.

The demo baseline in project.yaml is unchanged. Retargeting staging to local/order-operations-portal-staging and adding prod-demo are runtime topology versions in the ContextRail state directory, recorded in EB-017.
The server prints local_read_back=loopback in its startup line; the GitHub read-back and its UNVERIFIED status are unaffected.
cost_assumptions: No cloud resource and no model call: the EB-017 run uses CONTEXT_RAIL_ADVISOR=rule and only loopback HTTP.
One /healthz GET per non-replayed deployment attempt; nothing polls.
unknowns: config_drift is not observable from a local instance: /healthz does not report a config hash, and a local request may not declare deployed_config_hash, so the gate is always skipped for source "local". EB-017 does not exercise it.
Whether the demo baseline should eventually declare local target_refs and a prod-demo environment in project.yaml. That needs a Context Pack generator first.

Isolation between staging and prod-demo is process and port only: same machine, same user, same ContextRail state. Nothing stops an operator from pointing a prod-demo deployment at the staging port; the gates catch it (EB-017 attempt B), they do not prevent it.
The executable is hashed once at start; a binary replaced on disk between exec and the hash would be misreported (AI review finding, accepted as a narrow local race).
The single-operator waiver (AI review plus declared compensating controls) is what lets one person accept the candidate and approve both releases; a distinct human approver has not been exercised.

The build digest of the same demo source changes with every repository commit, because Go stamps vcs.revision and vcs.modified into the binary. A promotion therefore compares one build's bytes, as intended; it cannot show that two builds from different commits are the same program.
acceptance_criteria: The demo /healthz reports revision, build_digest and started_at, and a unit test compares build_digest with an independent sha256 of the test executable.

LocalReadBack rejects non-loopback hosts (including 10.0.0.1 and 169.254.169.254), non-http schemes, user info, query, fragment and an empty URL, never follows a redirect, and treats a non-200 answer as an observation, not an error (tests/release/local_readback_test.go).

A source "local" deployment that declares any identity field (revision, deployed_digest, deployed_target_ref, deployed_config_hash, smoke), lacks service_url, or runs on a server without an observer is rejected as an invalid request.

A real run (scripts/local-promotion.sh, EB-017) shows: staging PROMOTED with receipt RR-001; a same-key replay returning the same receipt without a new read; a prod-demo attempt against a different binary BLOCKED on digest_drift; a prod-demo attempt against the staging instance BLOCKED on target_drift and new_revision; a prod-demo attempt against the prod-demo instance PROMOTED with a receipt whose previous_receipt_id is RR-001.
go build ./..., go vet ./... and go test -count=1 ./... pass locally, and the demo module's go vet and go test pass; CI is cited only if a run is actually seen green.
